$comment: HMTc Comprehensive Testing Category Taxonomy v2.0 (2026-03-30). Source: /Users/karenpendergrass/Desktop/document_pdf.pdf. This file is the single source of truth for the 23-category structure that drives wiki/products/ scaffolding. Authored by K. Pendergrass, K. Eyer, D. Aleru.
organizing_principle: exposure pathway × regulatory jurisdiction, with user population (ages 0-5 vs general) as a secondary routing variable only where regulation explicitly distinguishes it

categories.name: Infant and Child Foods (Ages 0-5)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA (Closer to Zero), EU (Reg. 2023/915), Codex Alimentarius
boundary_rules: Product must be explicitly marketed/positioned for ages 0-5 or otherwise intended for infant/toddler feeding.
Categorization follows food matrix/type regardless of packaging format (pouch, jar, tub).
A snack marketed for toddlers routes here; the same base formulation marketed for general consumption routes to Categories 3-7.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA Closer to Zero action levels (Pb, iAs); EU Reg. 2023/915 (and amendments) MLs for Pb, Cd, iAs, Hg in infant/young child foods; Codex Alimentarius MLs for infant foods.

categories.name: Infant and Child Personal Care (Ages 0-5)
categories.exposure_pathway: Dermal (with incidental oral/mucosal for young children)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA cosmetics, CPSIA, state consumer product laws
boundary_rules: Product must be marketed for ages 0-5.
Baby shampoo routes here, not to Category 14 (Rinse-off Cosmetics), because infant dermal exposure assumptions (thin skin barrier, hand-to-mouth transfer) differ from adult.
Leave-on baby products (lotion, oil, powder) marketed for ages 0-5 route here, not to Category 13 (Leave-on Cosmetics).
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA cosmetics product-category codes; CPSIA total lead limits; California Prop 65 (Pb, Cd in children's products); EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.

categories.name: Grains, Cereals, and Rice Products
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Other grain products (oat, millet, quinoa, barley)

boundary_rules: Rice and non-rice subcategories are maintained as explicit pairs to support the Clean Counterpart Cap in the tightening formula.
Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 regardless of grain type.
A product that is primarily a grain product routes here. A mixed product (frozen lasagna) routes to Category 7.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Rice is a known contamination platform for iAs, Cd, and Pb. Non-rice grains are the clean counterpart.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA iAs action level for infant rice cereal (as reference benchmark for general rice); FDA Pb action level for foods; EU Reg. 2023/915 MLs for iAs in rice and rice products, Cd in cereals, Pb in cereals; Codex iAs ML for rice.

categories.name: Fruits, Vegetables, and Produce
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Fruit snacks (fruit leather, gummies not positioned as supplements)
Root/tuber vegetables (carrots, potatoes, beets, sweet potatoes)
Legumes/pulses (beans, lentils, chickpeas) and derived foods
Nut and seed butters (peanut butter, almond butter, tahini)

boundary_rules: Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1.
Root vegetables are a distinct subcategory because of cadmium accumulation from soil uptake.
Leafy greens are a distinct subcategory because of lead and cadmium accumulation.
A vegetable chip made primarily from root vegetables routes here. A mixed snack chip routes to Category 7.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Root vegetables and leafy greens are elevated for Cd and Pb via soil uptake pathways. Clean counterpart pairing: leafy greens (higher Cd) vs. non-root vegetables (lower Cd).
categories.regulatory_anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 MLs for Cd in vegetables (root vs. leafy vs. other), Pb in vegetables and fruits; Codex MLs for Pb in leafy vegetables; FDA Pb action levels for foods.

categories.name: Beverages
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Tea (when sold as conventional food with Nutrition Facts panel)

boundary_rules: Drinking water and mineral water route to Category 8 (Water), not here.
A tea with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16 (Dietary Supplements).
Plant milks route here; infant formula (plant-based) routes to Category 1.
Coffee routes here; a mushroom coffee sold as a supplement routes to Category 16.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Soy-based plant milks may carry elevated Al and Ni. Apple juice has specific Pb concerns. Tea leaves can accumulate Al.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA Pb action level in juice (including apple juice); EU Reg. 2023/915 for Pb and Cd in beverages, iAs in rice beverages; Codex MLs for beverages.

categories.name: Seafood
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Fish — marine, non-predatory (sardines, anchovies, salmon, cod)
Fish — marine, predatory (tuna, swordfish, shark, king mackerel)
Shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster, clams, oysters, mussels)
Seaweed/kelp foods (nori, wakame, kombu, dulse — as food products)

boundary_rules: Predatory fish are a distinct subcategory because methylmercury bioaccumulation increases with trophic level.
Seaweed is a distinct subcategory because of iAs and Cd accumulation.
A fish oil supplement for human consumption routes to Category 16 (Dietary Supplements).
A fish oil supplement for pet consumption routes to Category 18 (Pet Supplements).
Canned seafood carries the canned flag for tin monitoring in addition to Hg testing.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Predatory fish are a contamination platform for MeHg. Seaweed is a contamination platform for iAs and Cd. Non-predatory fish and shellfish are the clean counterparts for Hg.
categories.regulatory_anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 Hg MLs for fish (species-specific); FDA methylmercury action level (1.0 ppm in fish); Codex MeHg MLs for fish; EU iAs limits for seaweed; FDA Pb action levels for foods.

categories.name: Oils, Condiments, and Specialty Foods
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Other cooking oils (canola, sunflower, coconut, avocado, sesame)
Condiments (hot sauce, soy sauce, mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, salsa)
Cocoa/chocolate products (cocoa powder, dark chocolate, milk chocolate, chocolate chips)
Herbs/spices/dried seasonings (turmeric, cinnamon, paprika, oregano, cumin, chili powder, pepper)
Snacks (crackers, granola/snack bars, cookies, chips, popcorn — when not primarily a grain or produce product)
Canned foods, general (canned tomatoes, beans, soups — with tin flag)
Mixed meals/prepared foods (frozen dinners, boxed meals, ready-to-eat)

boundary_rules: Cocoa/chocolate is a distinct subcategory because cacao is a contamination platform for Cd and Pb.
Herbs/spices are a distinct subcategory because of known lead and chromium adulteration/contamination (especially turmeric, chili powder).
Canned foods carry the canned flag for tin monitoring regardless of the food matrix inside.
A product that is primarily a grain product (e.g., plain pasta) routes to Category 3. A mixed product (frozen lasagna) routes here.
Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Cacao → Cd, Pb (from soil); spices → Pb, Cr (from adulteration, processing); canned goods → Sn (from tinplate migration).
categories.regulatory_anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 for Cd in cacao/chocolate, Pb in spices and herbs, Sn in canned foods; FDA guidance on Pb in spices; Codex MLs for Pb in salt; FDA Pb action levels for foods.

categories.name: Water and Water-Based Products
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: EPA (MCLs), FDA (bottled water), EU (Drinking Water Directive)

subcategories.name: Infant water / nursery water (if not routed to Category 1 by age-marketing)

boundary_rules: Flavored water routes to Category 5 (Beverages), not here — flavoring changes the matrix and regulatory treatment.
Sparkling water with no flavoring or sweetener routes here.
This category has binding numeric limits for all 8 HMTc metals from multiple authorities — it is the most comprehensively regulated category in the taxonomy.
categories.regulatory_anchors: EPA Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs) for Pb, As, Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni (secondary standard); FDA 21 CFR 165.110 bottled water quality standards; EU Drinking Water Directive 2020/2184 (parametric values for Pb, As, Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni, Al).

categories.name: Infant and Child Contact Products (Ages 0-5)
categories.exposure_pathway: Oral (mouthing) + dermal (contact with mucous membranes, saliva)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: CPSIA, CPSC, FDA (food-contact for bottles/nipples), EU

subcategories.name: Sippy cups and toddler drinkware components

boundary_rules: Products in this category are defined by mouthing and contact exposure — the child puts the product in or near their mouth, or it contacts food/milk that the child ingests.
Bottles and nipples must meet FDA food-contact substance standards in addition to CPSIA.
A general-market reusable straw not marketed for children routes to Category 23 (Food-Contact Consumer Goods).
A teething toy routes here, not to Category 21 (Children's Toys) — the mouthing-specific exposure pathway governs.
categories.regulatory_anchors: CPSIA total lead limits; CPSC child care article definition; FDA food-contact substance regulations; EU food-contact material regulations; EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC migration limits.

categories.name: Infant and Child Durable Goods and Textiles (Ages 0-5)
categories.exposure_pathway: Dermal (prolonged skin contact) + incidental oral (mouthing of fabric, clasps)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: CPSIA, ASTM F963, OEKO-TEX, EU REACH

subcategories.name: Car seats (if retained in HMTc scope)
Clasps/fasteners (snaps, zippers, buttons) used in infant products

boundary_rules: Products in this category are defined by surface contact exposure — the child's skin contacts coatings, textiles, or structural materials for extended periods.
Analytical approach is surface wipe/extraction for coatings and substrate analysis for structural components.
Textiles are tested for extractable metals under conditions simulating sweat and saliva contact.
categories.regulatory_anchors: CPSIA total lead limits (100 ppm in accessible parts) and lead paint limits (90 ppm); ASTM F963 surface coating and substrate limits; CPSC durable infant/toddler product category list; OEKO-TEX Standard 100 (extractable metals in textiles); EU REACH Annex XVII restrictions; EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC.

categories.name: Meat, Poultry, and Eggs
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA, USDA (meat/poultry inspection), EU, Codex

subcategories.name: Processed meats (sausage, deli meat, bacon, hot dogs)

boundary_rules: Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 1 (mixed meals subcategory).
Organ meats/offal are tested as a subcategory of their respective animal type — organs may accumulate higher Cd and Pb than muscle meat.
Pet food containing meat/poultry routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods), not here.
categories.contamination_platform_notes: Organ meats (especially liver, kidney) accumulate Cd and Pb at higher levels than muscle tissue. Game meats may contain Pb from lead ammunition.
categories.regulatory_anchors: EU Reg. 2023/915 for Pb and Cd in meat, offal, and eggs; Codex MLs for Pb and Cd in meat; USDA/FSIS monitoring data as reference.

categories.name: Household Cleaning and Dishwashing
categories.exposure_pathway: Dermal (incidental skin contact) + ingestion (residue on dishes/surfaces)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: EPA (Safer Choice), Green Seal, state disclosure laws

subcategories.name: Floor finishes & strippers (if included in HMTc scope)
Other household specialty cleaners (by functional use-case)

boundary_rules: Fabric-intended products route to Category 19 (Laundry and Fabric-Contact).
Disinfectants/sanitizers are a distinct sub-scope (EPA-registered pesticide products) — if included, treat as a separate testing bucket within this category.
Dish soaps route here (they contact dishes, not fabric).
categories.regulatory_anchors: EPA Safer Choice product-type list; Green Seal GS-8 household cleaner scoping; CA SB 258 (Cleaning Product Right to Know Act); NY Household Cleaner Disclosure Act.

categories.name: Cosmetics and Personal Care — Leave-on
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA cosmetics, EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009

subcategories.name: Face/neck leave-on skin care (moisturizers, serums, night creams, leave-on masks)
Makeup — body/leg paints, bases, fixatives (including airbrush)
Eye makeup (liners, shadows, mascara, brow products, false lash adhesives, lash/eyebrow serums)
Deodorants (sticks, roll-ons, gels, creams, wipes, sprays)
Leave-on hair preparations (leave-in conditioners, tonics/dressings, styling aids, hair sprays, color sprays)
Permanent hair dyes/tints (remain in hair after application)
Manicuring preparations that remain on nails/skin (basecoats, polishes/enamels, cuticle softeners/creams)

boundary_rules: Product must remain on skin/hair/nails after application. If rinsed off, routes to Category 14.
Leave-on baby products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Category 2, not here.
A leave-in conditioner routes here. A rinse-out conditioner routes to Category 14.
A hair dye that remains in hair permanently routes here. A dye rinsed out after processing routes to Category 14.
Essential oil sold as topical leave-on skin treatment routes here.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA cosmetics product-category codes (leave-on tertiary categories); EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II (prohibited substances), Annex IV (colorants), Annex V (preservatives); California Prop 65 (Pb, Cd in cosmetics).

categories.name: Cosmetics and Personal Care — Rinse-off
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA cosmetics, EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009

subcategories.name: Facial cleansers (foaming, cream, gel, oil, micellar)

boundary_rules: Product must be applied to skin/hair and intentionally rinsed off after use.
Baby shampoo/body wash routes to Category 2 (Infant Personal Care), not here.
A leave-in conditioner routes to Category 13 (Leave-on), not here.
Intimate washes route to Category 15 (Feminine Care), not here — mucosal contact pathway overrides rinse-off classification.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA cosmetics product-category codes (rinse-off tertiary categories); EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009; Health Canada Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist.

categories.name: Feminine Care
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA (medical devices for tampons/pads/cups), EU MDR, FDA cosmetics

subcategories.name: Menstrual tampons (scented/unscented; applicator tested as distinct component)
Menstrual pads (disposable, panty liners, intralabial pads, reusable menstrual pads)
Period underwear and reusable menstrual garments
Douches and vaginal irrigation solutions/apparatus components

boundary_rules: Routing is governed by mucosal/intimate contact exposure pathway — not by product function or gender of user.
Intimate washes route here, not to Category 14, because vaginal mucosal exposure is a distinct and more permeable pathway than general skin contact.
A general body wash used incidentally in the intimate area does not route here — marketing and intended-use positioning determine routing.
categories.regulatory_anchors: 21 CFR Part 884 (tampons as Class II medical devices, pads including intralabial and reusable); FDA menstrual cup device classification; EU Medical Devices Regulation 2017/745; FDA cosmetics categories for douches/feminine deodorants.

categories.name: Dietary Supplements (Human)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA (DSHEA), USP, California Prop 65

subcategories.name: Oral solids: powders (bulk tubs, sachets, stick packs)
Food-like forms: teas (when labeled as supplement)
Food-like forms: bars (when labeled as supplement)
Ingredient class — oil-based supplements (fish oil/omega-3 and similar)

boundary_rules: Product must bear a Supplement Facts panel or be marketed/labeled as a dietary supplement under DSHEA.
FDA's definition requires supplements be ingested/swallowed — topical or inhaled products are excluded.
A product with a Nutrition Facts panel is a conventional food and routes to Categories 3-8.
A tea sold as conventional food routes to Category 5. The same tea with a Supplement Facts panel routes here.
Manuka honey with a Supplement Facts panel routes here. Regular honey routes to Category 7.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA DSHEA framework; USP <2232> elemental impurities limits; California Prop 65 MADLs (Pb MADL 0.5 µg/day as serving-based reference); NY AG consent decrees (precedent for Pb in supplements).

categories.name: Pet Foods
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA CVM, AAFCO, EU Directive 2002/32

subcategories.name: Milk replacers and specialty pet liquids

boundary_rules: Product must be intended for animal consumption as food, not as a supplement.
AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement or treat/snack positioning determines routing here.
Fish oil capsules for dogs route to Category 18 (Pet Supplements), not here.
categories.regulatory_anchors: AAFCO model regulations; FDA CVM guidance on pet food contaminants; EU Directive 2002/32 on undesirable substances in animal feed (Pb, As, Hg, Cd limits).

categories.name: Pet Supplements
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA CVM, NASC (voluntary), EU feed additive regulations
boundary_rules: Product is intended for animal consumption as a supplement — not as the sole or primary diet.
If a product bears an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement, it routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods).
A dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews subcategory) — primary function is food/treat, not supplementation.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA CVM compliance policies; NASC quality guidelines (voluntary, non-binding); EU feed additive regulations (Regulation 1831/2003).

categories.name: Laundry and Fabric-Contact Home Products
categories.exposure_pathway: Dermal (residue on fabric in prolonged skin contact)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: Green Seal GS-48, EPA Safer Choice

subcategories.name: Fabric protectants (excluding waterproofing/flame-retardant per GS-48 boundaries)

boundary_rules: Product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying, or treatment.
A carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning), not here — unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery.
Dryer sheets route here (fabric softener subcategory).
categories.regulatory_anchors: Green Seal GS-48 scope; EPA Safer Choice product types for laundry.

categories.name: Oral Care
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA (OTC drug monograph, cosmetics), ADA, EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009

subcategories.name: Floss and interdental cleaners (floss, picks, interdental brushes, woodsticks)
Oral irrigators/water flossers and tips (if included)
Denture and orthodontic-appliance care (adhesives, cleaning tablets/solutions)

boundary_rules: Primary site of exposure is the oral cavity → routes here, regardless of whether the product is regulated as a cosmetic, OTC drug, or device. Exposure pathway governs, not regulatory classification.
A whitening mouthwash with no drug claim is still Oral Care (oral cavity exposure), not Rinse-off Cosmetics.
A fluoride mouthwash is Oral Care, not Dietary Supplements.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA OTC drug monograph (for fluoride products); ADA acceptance program criteria; EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009 (toothpaste classified as cosmetic in EU); FDA cosmetics product-category codes (oral product types).

categories.name: Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: CPSC (ASTM F963, CPSIA, LHAMA), EU Toy Safety Directive

subcategories.name: Stuffed toys and bean bag-type toys
Pompoms and similar small fibrous craft items
Art & craft materials (paints, markers, crayons, colored pencils, inks, adhesives/glues, modeling clay, putties/gels/slimes, glitter/pigments, jewelry/craft kits)

boundary_rules: Product must be intended for children's play or creative activity.
Cross-reference: Teething toys/teethers are covered under Category 9 (Infant Contact Products), not this category.
Adult art supplies (professional-grade oil paint) are currently out of HMTc scope.
categories.regulatory_anchors: CPSC ASTM F963 toy-type mapping and requirements chart; CPSIA total lead limits (100 ppm) and lead paint limits (90 ppm); LHAMA/ASTM D-4236 for art materials; EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC (migration limits for metals).

categories.name: Home Air and Inhalation-Adjacent Products
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: RIVM, CPSC (candles), EU CLP

subcategories.name: Instant air refreshment sprays (aerosol cans, trigger sprays)
Replacement/refill materials for any dispensing system (oil refills, gel refills, spray refills)
Other home-air emission products (case-by-case, inhalation prioritized)

boundary_rules: Primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient air emission.
An essential oil sold as aromatherapy (inhaled via diffuser) routes here.
An essential oil sold as a topical skin serum (leave-on) routes to Category 13.
An essential oil sold as a dietary supplement (ingested) routes to Category 16.
Marketing/positioning determines routing when the same product could serve multiple functions.
categories.regulatory_anchors: RIVM air-freshener product-type list (exposure-factor framework); CPSC candle guidance on lead in metal-cored wicks; EU CLP Regulation (volatile chemical hazard classification).

categories.name: Food-Contact Consumer Goods and Kitchenware
categories.exposure_pathway: Ingestion (indirect — metals migrate/leach from product into food/beverage)
categories.regulatory_jurisdiction: FDA (food-contact substances), EU (food-contact material regulations), California Prop 65

subcategories.name: Metal and alloy cookware (cast iron, stainless steel, aluminum)

boundary_rules: Product must contact food during storage, preparation, cooking, or serving.
A cast iron pan routes here (metal and alloy cookware). A ceramic mug routes here (ceramicware).
A stainless steel water bottle routes here (metal bottles/tumblers). A water filter routes here.
Infant bottles/nipples route to Category 9 when marketed for ages 0-5 — even though they are food-contact items, the infant exposure pathway and regulatory treatment take priority.
categories.regulatory_anchors: FDA food-contact substance definitions (21 CFR Parts 170-199); EU food-contact material framework regulation (Regulation 1935/2004) and implementing measures; EU Annex I material-family list (Regulation 10/2011 for plastics, Directive 84/500/EEC for ceramics); FDA ceramics/lead leaching compliance policy guide; California Prop 65 (Pb/Cd in ceramicware, cookware).

novel_product_routing_protocol: Flag the product as 'unassigned — pending category review.'
Identify the primary exposure pathway (ingestion, dermal, inhalation, mucosal, indirect/migration).
Identify the applicable regulatory jurisdiction (FDA, EU, CPSC, EPA, etc.).
Determine whether the product fits an existing category with a boundary-rule clarification — if yes, update the boundary rules for that category and assign the product.

If no existing category can accommodate the product without distorting its scope — propose a new category with exposure pathway, regulatory anchors, and subcategories. The new category must be approved before any standards build begins.
No product is certified until its category assignment is resolved. An unassigned product does not default to a general or other bucket — it waits.
